elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Section 5.3(d) ("that is an Affiliate of the Depositor to whom the Depositor has assigned this Agreement, will be the successor to the Depositor") is untouched, and the amended Section 10.2(a) still opens "Except as stated in Sections 5.3, 7.4 and 7.6 (other than Section 7.6(d))" — the carve-out for Section 5.3 remains complete, so the Depositor's Affiliate route survives without consent. The new Issuer-consent proviso does not reach it.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Section 5.3(a)-(c) covers any Person into which the Depositor is merged or consolidated, resulting from such a merger or consolidation, or "succeeding to the Depositor's business," and Section 5.3 remains fully excepted from the Section 10.2(a) consent requirement. Only post-closing assumption/opinion/notice mechanics apply, not consent.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 10.2(a) now requires "the consent of the Issuer (not to be unreasonably withheld)" for assignment by the Servicer, and the exception list is narrowed by "(other than Section 7.6(d))", closing the Servicer's Affiliate no-consent route. Residual no-consent routes are Section 7.4 (Issuer-controlled Successor Servicer engagement) and Section 7.6(a)-(c) structural succession, which are successor events rather than voluntary assignments.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "consent of the Issuer (not to be unreasonably withheld)" is expressly inserted; the remaining unqualified consents (Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee, Certificateholders, 66-2/3% Controlling Class Noteholders) are third-party transaction consents, not Customer-side consents.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Added operative sentence: "The Servicer may not assign this Agreement to a competitor of the Issuer or the Depositor." The bar is unconditional and covers both Customer-side entities; "competitor" is used in its ordinary sense, matching the playbook's own preferred formulation.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Section 7.1 ("The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations") is retained unchanged, and no change-of-control trigger for the Servicer appears in the cited or rendered text; the condition of a Vendor exit right therefore does not arise.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Section 5.3(a)-(c) for the Depositor and Section 7.6(a)-(c) for the Servicer each preserve successor status on merger, consolidation or succession to business, and both remain excepted from Section 10.2(a) (the exception now excludes only Section 7.6(d)).

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Sections 5.3 and 7.6 each require, within fifteen (15) Business Days, delivery to the Issuer, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee of an Officer's Certificate and Opinion of Counsel and notice to the Rating Agencies — a written notification obligation, though it runs after the event and the Depositor owes no separate notice to the Servicer.

Section 5.3(d) is retained and remains fully excepted in Section 10.2(a): an Affiliate of the Depositor to whom the Depositor has assigned the Agreement becomes successor with no consent. Under the ASSIGN fallback rule, any retained no-consent non-successor exception (including an affiliate exception) defeats this element. To reach the fallback the drafter would have to narrow the Section 5.3 carve-out the same way Section 7.6(d) was narrowed — which is unnecessary here because the preferred level is already complete.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The inserted "(not to be unreasonably withheld)" qualifies the Issuer's consent in Section 10.2(a), which governs any assignment by the Depositor or the Servicer outside the carve-outs; the unqualified trustee/noteholder consents are third-party, not party, consents.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Not a fallback element; noted only for completeness — the added competitor bar is an extra beyond the fallback checklist but is required by the selected preferred level, so it does not offend minimality.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements are met, three by retained language (Sections 5.3, 7.1) and three by the two operations (Issuer consent not unreasonably withheld, exclusion of Section 7.6(d) from the carve-out, and the competitor bar).

The fallback is not complete (Section 5.3(d)'s retained no-consent affiliate route defeats "Other assignments require consent"), but that is immaterial because completeness at either level suffices and the preferred level is met.

Minimality holds: three targeted insertions into the existing Section 10.2(a) sentence plus one short new sentence; no favourable existing language (Sections 5.3, 7.1, 7.4, 7.6(a)-(c)) is deleted or paraphrased, and no survival tail, procedure or boilerplate is added.

Drafting refinement (not a minimality failure): the Issuer-consent proviso sits in a sentence binding "the Depositor or the Servicer," so it also formally attaches to the Depositor's non-carved-out assignments. The effect is nil because the Issuer is Customer-side and Section 5.3 remains fully carved out, but scoping the insertion to assignments "by the Servicer" would be cleaner if the counterparty objects.

Residual gap worth flagging in the rationale rather than re-drafting: Section 7.6(a)-(c) still lets a Person that merges with, or succeeds to the business of, the Servicer — potentially a competitor — become Servicer without Issuer consent, and the new competitor bar reaches only "assign," not structural succession. This is the mirror image of the Depositor's own Section 5.3 freedom, so symmetry supports leaving it.

Intent preserved: no dangling cross-reference (Section 7.6(d) still operates, now subject to consent), no contradictory retained sentence, and the trustee/noteholder consent architecture and 15-Business-Day assumption mechanics are untouched. "Competitor" is undefined but used in its ordinary sense, consistent with the playbook's preferred wording.
